newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures fall on data, yen snaps back.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures fall on data, yen snaps back.

text.p: IMM currency futures initially expanded opening losses after U.S. jobs data that was largely stronger-than-expected, but yen then snapped back up to the plus side as marks skidded even further.
Nonfarm payrolls rose 316,000 versus average forecasts for a 193,000-job increase. June's original 217,000 payrolls increase was revised upward to 228,000.
July's jobless rate fell to 4.8 percent from 5.0 percent in June and against forecasts for 4.9 percent.
But the critical average hourly earnings component stayed flat at $12.23 versus a forecasts for a 0.2-percent rise.
June U.S. personal income rose 0.6 pct and spending rose 0.3 percent against forecasts for 0.4-percent gain in each.
But most futures shaved losses as U.S. Treasury bond and stock marks tumbled after July national purchasing manager's index that rose to 58.6 versus forecasts for 56.1.
It showed gains in almost all sectors including prices, and that revived inflation concerns especially after the jump Thursday in the July Chicago purchaser's prices component.
But floor brokers said the jobs and NAPM data and ensuing drop in U.S. stocks and bonds simply may have limited currency downside for now rather than changed the fundamental outlook.
"The unemployment data as a whole, was it that bad? I don't think so," said one currency floor broker. "There may be some inflation down the road."

The yen bounced back partly on crosses with marks and on intervention nerves and talk of big dollar sellstops as the U.S. unit cleared the 119.00 threshold or about $0.008454 in September futures, floor brokers said.
Yen pressure had stemmed originally from a drop in July Japanese auto sales that reinforced ideas Japan's economy is still anemic.
Some said the next downside support in September marks, which slid to another new contract low at $0.5386 just before the NAPM report, stood at $0.5343 level.

At 1010 CDT/1510 GMT, September yen rose $0.000038 to $0.008519, marks lost $0.0055 to $0.5395, Swiss francs fell $0.0034 to $0.6604, sterling lost $0.0036 to $1.6336, Canadian dollar lost $0.0017 to $0.7258, Aussie dollar lost $0.0066 to $0.7401, and Mexican peso fell $0.000050 to $0.125550.
